title: Dependency Injection and Configuration
summary: Building applications from small services - constructor injection, the composition root, Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection with singleton, scoped and transient lifetimes, the generic host, configuration from appsettings.json, environment variables and user secrets bound to options classes, logging with ILogger, and how a container resolves constructors.

cards.a:
The one place near the program's start where objects are created and connected

Only the composition root knows which concrete classes are used; the rest of the code just receives its dependencies through constructors.

cards.q: Why should a singleton not depend on a scoped service?
cards.a:
The singleton lives for the whole app and would keep one scoped instance forever

A singleton is created once, so it captures the scoped instance it got first and shares it across all scopes. Being created on every request is what a transient service is.

cards.q: An environment variable `Reminders__Channel=sms` is set and appsettings.json says "email". Which value does configuration give?
cards.a:
sms

Environment variables are added after appsettings.json, so they override it; __ separates sections.
